paper_title: Revised constraints and Belle II sensitivity for visible and invisible axion-like particles
suggested_experiment_name: Combined ALP-photon constraints (SN1987A + beam dumps + colliders)
notes: Paper presents revised constraints and Belle II projected sensitivities for ALPs coupled to photons/hypercharge (g_agamma vs m_a, keV-GeV range). Coupling type is clearly AxionPhoton. However, all results are presented in figures (Fig 2, 4, 7) without tabulated numerical data points. No explicit (mass, coupling) table is available in the text, so no reliable data points could be extracted. Approximate values mentioned in text: SN1987A g_agamma < 6e-9 GeV^-1 for small masses; Belle II reaches ~1e-4 GeV^-1 over wide mass range; resonant freeze-out target ~1e-4 to 1e-5 GeV^-1. These are not a digestible curve. Both observed constraints (review) and projections (Belle II) are presented; flagged as projection since Belle II sensitivity is the central new result. 95% CL for most collider/beam dump, but Belle II projections quoted at 90% CL. | selector: figure_vision (sole candidate) | Vision: Figure 2 left panel (g_aZ=0). The lower boundary of the combined excluded region is traced. At low masses (keV-MeV) the boundary is set by SN 1987A (a->gamma gamma), rising through SN1987A and electron beam dumps. A gap/peak appears near m_a ~ 0.3-0.5 GeV where the beam dump sensitivity ends, then collider constraints (e+e-->gamma gamma, proton beam dumps) take over at higher masses around g~5e-5. Multiple overlapping constraints make precise lower-envelope tracing approximate.
